title: Sharp Variance Inflation under Uniform Roster Sampling in Therapist Trials with Fixed Capacities
banked_reason: Typed math and decision pass; sharp heterogeneous-capacity factor J is sound, but paper_score_ceiling 6.4 < field threshold 7.4 caps final tier at incremental, with salvageable=false. Independent main validity confirms novelty-floor stop.
gap_reasons: The delivered theorem establishes the exact worst-graph factor J, including fixed heterogeneous capacities, through an all-table upper bound and a bounded attaining table; the cited preservation and Hessian results cover their uses ([Borcea–Brändén–Liggett](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.2340), [Brändén–Huh](https://arxiv.org/html/1902.03719v8)). The framing accurately distinguishes this sharp endpoint from the unresolved graph-only extremizer classification, so no stale sharpness overclaim requires correction. The contribution concerns one uniform static-roster sampler, one prescribed variance proxy, and its graph-induced fixed-policy estimand, which limits its broader econometric significance. The exact certificate remains exponential, and the delivered computations check small synthetic cases without establishing operational performance or correction magnitudes for realistic nonextremal eligibility structures. The batch interval supplies coverage under separate independence, boundedness, and variance-divergence conditions, but its standard concentration and Lyapunov arguments add limited methodological significance. These constraints support a field contribution while holding the projected leading-journal paper score to 6.4. proof_attempt_summary: Proved the sharp worst-eligibility-graph factor J informally, then generalized equal capacity to every prespecified heterogeneous even-capacity vector and improved exact rational PSD certification to cubic decision cost. Math and decision panels passed with no findings after primary-source verification, but the projected paper score 6.4 stayed below the field threshold 7.4 and capped achieved tier at incremental; independent main validity confirmed no bounded same-kernel salvage. No Lean formalization, promotion, presentation, or git commit was entered; graph-only extremizer classification remains an explicit optional open problem.
tldr: For \(J\ge2\) fixed named therapists and prespecified integer replications \(\rho_j\ge2\), sample uniformly all legal static-eligibility rosters of capacities \(c_j=2\rho_j\), then assign \(\rho_j\) patients per arm at therapist \(j\). For deterministic bounded potential outcomes, the sharp worst-graph variance correction is \(\Gamma_{\boldsymbol\rho}(J)=J\). A connected mobile-patient cycle attains it for every capacity vector. Completion-weighted stable membership marginals supply the upper bound; exact counting and rational triangular elimination certify graph-specific corrections including singular directions. Complete eligibility has correction one; its equal-capacity specialization recovers the binary permutation assignment law of Walwyn et al. The supporting independent-batch interval uses the prespecified all-two vector in every batch and retains its separate variance and concentration conditions.
gap: Crossed therapist designs leave prospective capacity and availability extensions, while general optimized variance-bound theory does not evaluate the worst scalar correction for uniform legal rosters and the prescribed within-therapist estimate.
fill: The proposed result pairs an all-table upper bound with a legal bounded response attainer and an exact graph-specific certificate. The supporting batch interval retains the same policy-based causal contrast in each prespecified experiment.
